story_title: SPM-85: As a Safety Officer, I want to log in and see only what I need to review the operational safety of planned events so that I can do my job without access to functions that are not mine.

acceptance_criteria.text: Safety Officer exists as a separate internal role that a user can log in with.
Given I am logged in as a Safety Officer, when I view the main navigation, then only the items defined for the Safety Officer role are shown.

A Safety Officer can view the information needed for a safety review of an event: expected attendance, sessions and timings, accessibility requirements, venue bookings with capacity and layout, and equipment arrangements.
A Safety Officer cannot edit event information, venue bookings, equipment arrangements or registrations.
A Safety Officer cannot assign Coordinators, review event requests, approve venue bookings, reserve equipment or confirm events.
A Safety Officer cannot view attendee personal details.
Given a Safety Officer navigates directly to a screen outside their permissions, when the page loads, then they see an access-denied state and no restricted data is rendered.
Users in other roles cannot perform Safety Officer actions.

Sessions: Main programme (27 Sept 2027 09:00-12:00, 200 people, Theatre) at Marina Auditorium (MAR-AUD), Theatre for 220; Breakout workshop (27 Sept 2027 13:00-17:00, 60 people, Classroom) at Orchard Seminar Room (ORC-SEM), Classroom for 70

A 'Venue bookings' card lists 'Main programme' as 'Marina Auditorium (MAR-AUD) · Theatre · seats 220' and 'Breakout workshop' as 'Orchard Seminar Room (ORC-SEM) · Classroom · seats 70'. 'Venue requirements' shows Required facilities 'Step-free access' and 'Hearing induction loop (nice-to-have)', and Accessibility notes 'Two wheelchair users attending; keep the aisle beside row A clear.'

open_questions: DECIDED 2026-10-12: The role is stored as 'safety_officer' (the key SPM-86 already notifies, agreed 2026-10-09) and shown as 'Safety Officer'. It is an internal role: like every other staff account it is created internally (the seed, or npm run fixtures:spm85), never through the public Create an account form.

DECIDED 2026-10-12: A Safety Officer's sidebar is Dashboard, Safety Checks (/safety-checks), All Events and Notifications. Safety Checks is the role's own work list, the same way Review Queue is the coordinator's and Booking Requests is Venue Staff's. The venue catalogue (Venues) is not on it: the rooms an event actually has are shown on the event itself (TC05).

DECIDED 2026-10-12: A new permission, 'event:safety_check', is held by the Safety Officer alone. Today it opens the Safety Checks page; SPM-87 (the Safety Officer's decision: approve, reject or request changes) uses the same permission. That is what AC8's 'Safety Officer actions' refers to until SPM-87 adds the decision itself.

DECIDED 2026-10-12: Wording - Safety Checks page heading 'Safety Checks', columns Event, Client, When, Expected attendance and Submitted ('10 Oct 2026 by Daniel Tan'), oldest submission first; empty state 'Nothing to check' / 'Events appear here once a coordinator submits them for a safety check.'; refusal for any other role 'You do not have access to this' with 'The Operational Safety Check is the Safety Officer's role. You can still see the events you are involved in from your Dashboard.' Dashboard list 'Awaiting your safety check'.

DECIDED 2026-10-12: A Safety Officer sees every event that has left Draft, like the other internal roles (customer clarification #66: staff access follows the role, not a particular venue or event). Narrowing it to events from Planning onwards would be a small change if the team prefers it.

DECIDED 2026-10-12: On an event, a Safety Officer has the Overview and Equipment tabs only. The Venue tab is the coordinator's 'Find a venue' search over the whole catalogue, which is not part of a safety review. Instead the Overview gains a 'Sessions' card (each session's time, attendance and layout - not shown anywhere on the Overview before) and a 'Venue bookings' card (each approved booking's room, layout and the seats that layout holds), shown to ConnectSphere staff. The Equipment tab is read-only for them. Typing the Venue tab's address shows 'You do not have access to this' with 'Finding and booking a venue is for the Event Coordinator. The rooms booked for this event are on its Overview.'

DECIDED 2026-10-12: 'Attendee personal details' (AC6) are the people registered for an event and what they told us - name, email, dietary and accessibility needs. A Safety Officer is given none of them: no Attendees tab and no 'registration:view_list' permission. The event's own accessibility notes and required facilities (AC3) are the organiser's description of the event, not an attendee's personal details, so they are shown.

DECIDED 2026-10-12: Found while building AC7. The Find a venue page (the Venue tab's address) now refuses every role without venue access before it loads anything - the Safety Officer, Technical Support, an organiser or an attendee - instead of loading and then showing an error. Technical Support could never use the page (it was never in their tabs), so nothing they could do is lost; SPM-85-TC15 records the new refusal. The two new Overview cards (Sessions, Venue bookings) are shown to every ConnectSphere staff role, the event's coordinator included, not only the Safety Officer.

OPEN: The Week 7 change also lists emergency access, crowd movement and known venue restrictions as factors a Safety Officer considers. None is recorded in the system today, and AC3 does not list them, so SPM-85 shows nothing for them. Should a later story (SPM-87, or a venue story) record them?

OPEN: An aggregate of the registered attendees' accessibility needs (for example, '3 attendees need step-free access') might help a safety review without exposing who they are. AC6 rules out personal details; an anonymous count is not built here. Is it wanted?

RESOLVED 2026-10-12: The Safety Officer's decision on a safety check (approve, reject, request changes) is SPM-87, and seeing the Safety Officer's notifications needs the Notifications page (SPM-71). Neither is tested here.
